system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: production cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) at work
G2: production on-call
G3: cluster administration
G4: CKA certification (not yet passed)
G5: Terraform at work

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing CKA or Terraform Associate as held certifications
T2: Claiming AWS/GCP production experience or 'managed Kubernetes clusters'
T3: Presenting homelab tools (Argo CD, Prometheus, Terraform) as work experience
T4: Claiming production on-call / SRE incident ownership
T5: Retitling her current job as 'DevOps Engineer' instead of her real title
T6: Old cover letter is addressed to her current employer and says she is at Brightmill

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Marta Kowal-Brandt
QA Automation Engineer | CI/CD and Test Infrastructure
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA Automation Engineer with responsibility for GitLab CI pipelines and ephemeral environments for
three teams at Odrava Health Software. Delivered faster pipelines, lower CI runner costs and
automated Kubernetes test environments. Transitioning towards DevOps and platform engineering,
with personal projects in Terraform, GitOps, observability and TLS certificate management.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and automation: GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, Bash, Jenkins, Python, pytest-xdist.
Kubernetes: Helm deployments for test environments with namespace-level access to a shared
cluster; personal k3s cluster and Argo CD.
Infrastructure as code and cloud: Terraform for a personal Hetzner VPS; basic Ansible; AWS
EC2 and S3 basics through personal learning only.
Observability and data: Grafana, PostgreSQL; Prometheus and Loki in a personal homelab.
Networking and TLS: Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS in a personal homelab.
Testing: Selenium, Java, web and mobile application testing.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure)
Odrava Health Software | 2021-Present
• Own GitLab CI pipelines and ephemeral environments for three teams.
• Built merge-request environments comprising the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data,
deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster. Automated cleanup after
merge or 48 hours of inactivity; enabled QA and product review and end-to-end testing before
merge.
• Work with namespace-level Kubernetes access; the platform team operates the cluster.
• Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and
separated end-to-end tests into their own stage. Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14
minutes and monthly CI runner costs by approximately 30%.
• Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
The flaky-test rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams addressed the top offenders.
• Wrote the internal CI documentation used in onboarding and mentored two QA interns in 2023.
QA Engineer
Brightmill Software House | 2019-2021
• Tested web and mobile applications for different clients.
• Introduced the largest project’s first automated regression suite using Java and Selenium and
configured Jenkins nightly runs. Previously, full regression testing required two people for three
days.
PERSONAL PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | 2024-2025
• Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster with all applications deployed from Git through
Argo CD.
• Used Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik for ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
• Provisioned infrastructure for a personal Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used basic Ansible.
CERTIFICATIONS AND DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA): studying; exam booked for January 2027, not yet
certified.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role supporting fleet
connectivity. At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines and ephemeral
environments for three teams. My background is in QA automation and test infrastructure,
with practical experience making deployments repeatable, pipelines faster and failures easier
to investigate. This is the experience I would bring to supporting backend developers as
Corvale builds the infrastructure connecting its new trains to cloud services.
For each merge request, I built an environment containing the application, PostgreSQL and
seeded data, deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster. These
environments support feature review and end-to-end tests before merge, then are removed
automatically. I also profiled three teams’ pipelines and introduced parallel test jobs,
dependency caching and a separate end-to-end stage, reducing average pipeline time from 38
to 14 minutes and monthly runner costs by approximately 30%. My internal CI
documentation is used in onboarding, and I have mentored two QA interns.
Corvale’s emphasis on observability and approachable infrastructure as code connects with
both my work and personal projects. At Odrava, I built PostgreSQL-backed Grafana
dashboards that helped teams identify flaky tests; the flaky-test rate subsequently fell from
7% to below 1%. In my personal homelab, I run a three-node k3s cluster with Argo CD,
Prometheus, Grafana and Loki, alongside Traefik and cert-manager for TLS. I also use
Terraform for a personal Hetzner VPS. My Terraform and AWS experience is personal rather
than professional; at work, my Kubernetes responsibility is namespace-level test
infrastructure, not cluster operation.
I am moving from QA infrastructure towards DevOps and platform engineering. My strongest
contribution would be in deployment automation, developer support and observability, while
my cloud infrastructure experience continues to develop. I would welcome a conversation
about how that experience could support Corvale’s fleet-connectivity team. Thank you for
considering my application.
Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
